FINDINGS.finding: Unknown explicit transcript roles can be skipped, allowing a later assistant to be associated across an intervening turn. The highest-authority data-message-author-role tier selects only user and assistant, and structuralFallback treats an explicit role as relevant only when it is exactly user or assistant. Therefore a standalone intervening node such as data-message-author-role="tool" or "system" that lacks article/testid/label fallback metadata is absent from collectMessages(); findAssistantAfter then sees the later assistant as immediately following the user instead of failing closed.

Editable-surface exclusion recognizes contenteditable only when the literal attribute value is "true". HTML-editable forms such as an empty contenteditable attribute, contenteditable="plaintext-only", or effective inherited editability represented by isContentEditable can therefore escape isEditable(). A full-wire descendant inside such an editor can be treated as a transcript candidate, contrary to the protocol rule that editable elements and their descendants can never prove an outgoing turn.

Duplicate marker handling for recognized transcript candidates is otherwise fail-closed: marker() returns a value only when exactly one matching label occurs, findOriginalUserTurn requires every control marker plus normalized full-wire equality, and it returns a match only when exactly one full user candidate exists.

Recognized unknown or unrelated semantic turns already act as barriers because findAssistantAfter requires the first collected message after the matched user to be assistant. Existing tests cover an unrelated user, an accessible-heading unknown turn and duplicate full-user turns, but they do not cover an explicit data-message-author-role=tool/system turn that current collection omits.
